title: Advisory
description: A normalized vulnerability/patch advisory record from a content source (Phase 5). Global content — advisories are NOT tenant-scoped (see docs/adr/0010-global-content-catalogue.md). Known fields are closed so typos are caught; per-source extras go in the open 'sourceMetadata' objects, so Phase 5 can extend without a frozen-contract change.

externalId.description: The source's identifier, e.g. CVE-2025-12345, USN-1234-1, RHSA-2025:0001. Unique per (source, externalId).

severity.description: 'unknown' is a first-class value: a source that does not state severity must never be made to fabricate one (HARD-PROBLEMS #8).

withdrawnAt.description: Set when the source retracts the advisory. Content retires; it is never deleted.

cvss.description: Structured so the score is auditable: a bare number cannot say which version or vector produced it (DIFFERENTIATORS #4).

source.description: Which content source supplied this score (NVD and a vendor may disagree).

kev.description: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities membership. Absent/null means 'not evaluated'; listed:false means 'evaluated, not on the list'.

epss.description: EPSS exploit-prediction scoring. Both values are probabilities in [0,1], not percentages.

provenance.description: REQUIRED. One entry per contributing source, so every input to a risk score is traceable to who said it and when (DIFFERENTIATORS #4, Phase 5 exit criteria). An advisory assembled from NVD + KEV + EPSS carries three entries.

sourceRecordId.description: The record's id within that source, when it differs from externalId.

contentHash.description: Hash of the raw source payload, so a later re-fetch can prove whether the source changed.

rawRef.description: Pointer to the retained raw source payload (path/URI), not the payload itself.

ecosystem.description: Selects the version comparator (HARD-PROBLEMS #3). Constrained to the three implemented comparators — a fourth ecosystem needs a comparator, so widening this is the correct gate.

platform.description: The release/product this fix statement applies to, RAW as sourced: 'ubuntu:22.04', 'rhel:9', 'debian:12', 'windows:server-2022'. One advisory commonly fixes the same package at DIFFERENT versions per release (one USN covers every supported Ubuntu release), so this is part of the row's identity. NULL when the source states no release scope (e.g. NVD CPE ranges) — never a fabricated sentinel. See docs/adr/0011-fixed-version-raw-as-sourced.md.

fixedVersion.description: RAW as sourced — never parsed, split, or canonicalized at ingest ('3.0.2-0ubuntu1.16', '0:1.2.3-4.el9_3', '10.0.19045.4046'). The Phase 6 per-ecosystem comparator owns interpretation. NULL when no fix is available yet. See docs/adr/0011-fixed-version-raw-as-sourced.md.

backported.description: True when the distro backported the fix without an upstream version bump (HARD-PROBLEMS #2).

sourceMetadata.description: Open extension point. Per-source fields that do not belong in the normalized contract live here, so Phase 5 can carry them WITHOUT a frozen-contract change (review H2) while the known fields above stay closed against typos.
